problem: The area of a square decreases at a rate of $12\,{\text{in}}^{2}\text{/min}.$ If $x$ and $A$ denote the side length and area of the square, respectively, then find an expression for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$, where $t$ is the time in minutes.

feedback.problem: The area of a square decreases at a rate of $56{\text{ m}}^{2}\text{/s}.$ At what rate are the lengths of the sides of the square decreasing when the sides are $8\text{ m}$ long?
feedback.worked_solution:
Here, the area is changing at a constant rate,  and we want to know the rate at which the side lengths are changing.

First, let's draw a diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14095797/assets/1cb323f4c38bb4fc13ffc81f47544424872480b42f033032da47c04d097e8696.png)

We want to find $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ The area $A$ is related to side length $x$ by the formula

$$
A={x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2x\end{aligned}
$$

We know from the given information that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =-56\text{ m}{}^{2}\text{/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this information, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}-56 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2x \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{28}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when the sides are $8\,\text{m},$ we have $x=8.$ Substituting this information into the above, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{28}{8}=-\frac{7}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the lengths of the sides are decreasing at a rate of $\frac{7}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$
